body:
My note from at dusk: the field trial crew carried rinsed gloves. my brother started coughing. I had not yet heard that the siren began.

The first account was spoken quickly, as if there might be a bus to catch. I wrote it down before another person could replace it.

The person who was supposed to collect it had no time to stop. I did not put it back with the rest of the ordinary papers.
title: At dusk: rinsed gloves

body:
I told them the barn was empty after the morning count. It was true if you counted people. The two calves were still there, and I could hear the smaller one pressing its head against the gate whenever a truck stopped outside.

A man I had never seen asked for the ledger, then asked whether I kept another. I said the kitchen calendar had the births on it. He took that too. By evening the gate had a new chain. Nobody asked me to feed them, and nobody said I could go back in.

I left the milk pail by the door because I thought a person who came to lock it would see it. In the morning the pail was gone. The chain was still there.
title: Count the calves as absent
